newsitem.title: USA: FAA to call for Boeing 737 rudder modifications.
newsitem.headline: FAA to call for Boeing 737 rudder modifications.

text.p: Federal safety officials said they will announce on Wednesday proposed rudder modifications to the popular Boeing Co 737, the type of jet involved in two still unexplained fatal crashes.

But industry sources said that rudder problems are not a suspected cause of the crashes at Pittsburgh in 1994 and at Colorado Springs in 1991 -- although in both cases the 737s went down after going into sudden and uncontrolled rolls.
The modifications follow Boeing recommendations last November that all of the approximately 2,700 737s flying worldwide be tested for a potential rudder safety problem.
Boeing and National Transportation Safety Board investigators had found the 737 rudder power control could jam when subjected to unusually extreme temperatures.

But the board has yet to fix the cause of the two crashes, and sources said there was no reason to think the rudder changes would prevent any future crashes similar to those at Pittsburgh and Colorado Springs.

Boeing said its tests showed that if the 737 rudder power control did jam, the plane could roll in one direction and possibly go out of control if the pilot did not take the right action or if the plane were too close to the ground.
The problem had never been encountered in the some 69 million flights of the 737s flying worldwide, Boeing said.
In Pittsburgh, all 132 people aboard the USAir Group Inc flight were killed. A total of 25 people were killed in the Colorado Springs plane flown by United Airlines, a unit of UAL Corp.
